title: Install-mode call machine
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean words, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ within $T(|a|)$ steps on every input $a$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $C$, entry and exit states of $C$, and a natural number $c$ with at least one work tape such that, for every pair of Boolean words $x,a$, starting from the clean seam on native input $x$ with $a$ on the first work tape and the other work tapes blank, $C$ reaches the clean seam with $f(a)$ on the first work tape and the other work tapes blank at some positive time $t\\le c(T(|a|)+|a|+|f(a)|+1)$. The exit state is not visited at any earlier positive time before $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean words
$f$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
$M$ computes $f$ within $T(|a|)$ steps for every input $a$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a bundled finite machine computing a function $f$ on Boolean words in time
$T$. Then there are a machine $C$ with a positive number of work tapes, control states
called entry and exit, and a constant $c$ such that for every native input $x$ and
argument $a$: starting $C$ at the canonical seam in the entry state with $a$ as the sole
tape-resident word (all other tapes blank, input head at one, empty output), there is a
positive time $t \le c\,(T(|a|) + |a| + |f(a)| + 1)$, before which the exit state is
never visited, at which $C$ is exactly at the canonical seam in the exit state carrying
$f(a)$ as the sole tape-resident word: the result installed, all scratch restored,
nothing emitted, and the native input untouched.
